beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Why the World Won’t End offers conditional hope without claiming catastrophe is impossible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It separates the end of a familiar world from the extinction of humanity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book takes serious hazards seriously while questioning the certainty that apocalypse stories encourage.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central concern is what a civilization must preserve so that learning can continue after disruption.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a way to examine danger without confusing survival with a good future.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A sudden catastrophe and a slow loss of adaptive capacity create different problems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book compares hazards through their mechanisms rather than ranking them by dramatic appeal.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks what can harm many people, break technological continuity, or threaten the species itself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These categories must stay distinct if preparation is to match the actual danger.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The comparison turns an emotional argument about the end into a more specific inquiry.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The institutional chapters examine decisions made when no leader holds the whole system in mind.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Distributed knowledge makes civilization capable, while fragmented responsibility can make correction difficult.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Resilience may preserve useful abilities without preserving freedom or humane social arrangements.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book therefore connects preparedness with dissent, memory, pluralism, and the capacity to rebuild.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its adolescent-species image remains a metaphor for uneven maturity, rather than a biological prediction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the note about the title before reading its survey of serious hazards.
